newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures and interest rate futures settled little changed on Wednesday after a calm session ahead of a French public holiday on Thursday.

Traders said the market would trade in the same range of the past few sessions unless an opinion poll of voters' intentions for the May 25/June 1 election showed a marked shift to the left in which case there would be a decline.
The June bond future settled at 129.52, up 0.04, after hitting a high of 129.66, the same as on Tuesday. Traders said few were taking new positions with most just content to play technical levels.
Traders said the market would be very quiet on Friday as many in France would be on holiday.

The two polls out since the market closed on Tuesday were both viewed as reassuring for the French markets as they suggested the centre-right coalition would still hold a majority in the National Assembly.

There was little action in the cash market on Wednesday, although some said the two-year part of the curve was coming under slight pressure from those putting on curve flatteners ahead of the auction, which in turn boosted the 10-year area relative to German bonds.
The Treasury sold 451 million Ecu of the 5.5 percent 2007 OATs with a healthy cover of 3.1, demand being helped by recent underperformance relative to French franc OATs.
As expected the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent for Friday's same-day money market tender after its monetary policy council meeting.
